nodes.name: Theorem 1.1
nodes.statement:
Let $M$ be a $(2n+1)$-manifold, $A\subset M$ be a closed set, and
     $\xi$ be an almost contact structure on $M$.
    If $\xi$ is genuine on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A\subset M$ then $\xi$ is homotopic relative to $A$ to a genuine contact structure.
    In particular, any almost contact structure on a closed manifold is homotopic to a genuine contact structure.

nodes.name: Proposition 3.8: Prop
nodes.statement: Every neighborhood of an overtwisted disc in a contact manifold contains a foliation by overtwisted discs.

nodes.name: Theorem 3.12
nodes.statement:
Let $T = D^q$ and $A \subset M$ be a closed subset such that $M \setminus A$ is connected, and let 
  ${}^T\xi$ be a fibered almost contact structure on ${}^T M$ which is genuine on 
  $(T\times {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A) \cup (\partial T\times M)$.
  If there exists a fixed overtwisted disc $(D_{\mathrm{ot}}, \eta_{\mathrm{ot}}) \subset M\setminus A$ such that for all
  $\tau \in T$ the inclusion $(D_{\mathrm{ot}}, \eta_{\mathrm{ot}}) \subset (M \setminus A, \xi^\tau)$ is a contact embedding,
  then ${}^T\xi$ is homotopic   to a fibered genuine contact structure   through fibered almost contact structures
fixed on $\big(T\times (A\cup D_{\mathrm{ot}})\big)\cup\big(\partial T\times M\big)$

nodes.name: Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement:
The inclusion map induces an isomorphism
 $$j_*:\pi_0(\mathfrak{Cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(M;A,\xi_0))\to\pi_0(\mathfrak{cont}(M;A,\xi_0))$$
 and moreover the map
 $$j:\mathfrak{Cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(M;A,\xi_0,\phi)\to\mathfrak{cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(M;A,\xi_0,\phi)$$ is a (weak) homotopy  equivalence.

nodes.name: Proposition 3.9: Prop
nodes.statement:
Let $K_0, K, \;K_0\geq K,$ be two contact Hamiltonians and $K$ is special. Then
the contact shell $(B_{K_0}\# B, \eta_{K_0} \# \xi)$
given by performing a boundary connected sum at the north pole of $B_{K_0}$ and the south pole of $D_{K} \subset \partial B$
is equivalent to a genuine contact structure.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.3
nodes.statement:
Let $K:\Delta_{\rm cyl} \to {\mathbb{R}}$ a special contact Hamiltonian and define
	$$
		K_{\delta}: \Delta_\delta \to {\mathbb{R}} \quad\mbox{by}\quad K_{\delta}:= K + (\delta-1).
	$$
	If $\delta < 1$ is sufficiently close to $1$, then 
	$\tilde{K}_\delta:= (C_\delta)_* K_{\delta} : \Delta_{{\rm cyl}} \to {\mathbb{R}}$ is also a special contact Hamiltonian.

nodes.name: Proposition 3.11: Prop
nodes.statement:
Let $(K_0, \Delta_{{\rm cyl}})$ be a contact Hamiltonian and consider the fibered contact shell 
	$$({}^TB_{K_0} \# {}^TB, {}^T\eta_{K_0} \# {}^T\xi)$$
	given by performing a boundary connected sum on each fiber over $\tau \in T$ at the north pole of 
	$B_{K^{(\delta(\tau))}_0}$ and the south pole of $D_{K} \subset \partial B$.  If $K \leq K_0$ is special, then
	$({}^TB_{K_0} \# {}^TB, {}^T\eta_{K_0} \# {}^T\xi)$ is fibered equivalent to a  genuine fibered contact structure.

nodes.name: Lemma 9.1
Proposition 3.1: Prop
nodes.statement:
For fixed dimension $2n+1$ there exists a contact Hamiltonian $(K_{\mathrm{univ}}, \Delta_{{\rm cyl}})$,
 specified in Lemma 8.7, such that the following holds. 
 For any almost contact manifold $(M, \xi)$ as in Theorem 1.1
  there exists an almost contact structure $\xi'$ on $M$, which is homotopic   to $\xi$ relative $A$ through almost contact structures,
and a finite collection of
 disjoint balls $B_i\subset M\setminus A$ for $i=1,\dots, L$, with piecewise smooth boundary such that
 \begin{itemize}
 \item $\xi'$ is a genuine contact structure on $M\setminus \bigcup_1^L{\rm Int\,} B_i$
 \item the contact shells $\xi'|_{B_i}$ are equivalent to
 $(B_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}},\eta_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}})$
 for $i=1, \dots, L$.
 \end{itemize}

nodes.name: Lemma 5.4: Prop
Proposition 5.3: Prop
nodes.statement:
The fibered family of contact shells ${}^I \zeta$ is homotopic relative to
$$
	{\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{s = 0\} \cup \bigcup_{s \in [0,1]} {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial(B_{K^{(s)}}\# {\bf B}) \subset {}^I B_{K}\# {}^I {\bf B}
$$
through fibered families of contact shells on ${}^I B_{K}\# {}^I {\bf B}$ to a fibered family of genuine contact structures.

nodes.name: Proposition 3.10: Prop
nodes.statement:
Let $T = D^q$ and let $A \subset M$ be a closed subset.
Every fibered almost contact structure ${}^T\xi_0$ on ${}^TM = T \times M$
that is genuine on $(T\times{\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A)\cup ({\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial T \times M)$ is homotopic relative to 
$(T\times A) \cup (\partial T \times M)$ through fibered almost contact structures on ${}^TM$ 
to some structure ${}^T\xi$ with the following property:

There is a collection of disjoint  embedded fibered shells ${}^{T_i}B_i \subset {}^TM$ 
 over (not necessarily disjoint) $q$-dimensional discs $T_i \subset T$ for $i = 1, \dots, L$ such that 
\begin{enumerate}
	\item 
	the fibers of ${}^T\xi$ are genuine contact structures away from $\bigcup_{i=1}^L {\rm Int\,}({}^{T_i} B_i)$ and
	\item the fibered contact shells
	$({}^{T_i}B_i, {}^{T_i}\xi)$ and $({}^{T_i} B_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}}, {}^{T_i}\eta_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}})$
	are equivalent.
\end{enumerate}
Furthermore for every $C \subset \{1, \dots L\}$ the intersection $\bigcap_{i \in C} T_i$ either empty or a disc.

nodes.name: Proposition 6.2: Prop
nodes.statement:
Let $M$ be a $(2n+1)$-manifold,  $A\subset M$ a closed subset, and
  $\xi_0$   an almost contact structure on $M$ that is genuine on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A\subset M$. There exists a finite number of embedded saucers $B_i\subset M$ for $i=1, \dots, N$ such that  $\xi_0$ is homotopic relative to $A$ to an almost contact structure $\xi_1$ which is genuine on $M\setminus\bigcup_{i=1}^N B_i$ and whose restriction to each saucer $B_i$ is semi-contact and regular.

nodes.name: Proposition 6.12: Prop -> [uul]
nodes.statement:
If $(B, \xi) = \sigma_\phi$ is a regular semi-contact saucer viewed as a shell,
then there is a time-independent contact Hamiltonian $K:\Delta\to{\mathbb{R}}$
such that $(B, \xi)$ dominates the circle model contact shell $(B_K, \eta_K)$.

nodes.name: Proposition 6.13: Prop
nodes.statement:
Let $({}^TB, {}^T\xi)$ be a fibered  regular semi-contact saucer,
then there exists a family of time-independent  contact Hamiltonians
$K^\tau:\Delta\to{\mathbb{R}}$ for $\tau\in T$  which satisfy $K_\tau>0$ for $\tau\in \partial T$, such that $({}^TB, {}^T\xi)$ dominates the corresponding fibered  circle model contact shell $({}^TB_K, {}^T\eta_K)$.

nodes.name: Proposition 7.6: Prop
nodes.statement:
Let $ M$ be a $(2n+1)$-manifold and $A\subset M$ a closed set, so that  $M\setminus A$ is connected. Let ${}^T\xi_0$ be a fibered almost contact structure on ${}^TM$ which is genuine on $(T\times{\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A)\cup (\partial T\times  M)\subset T\times M$. Then there exist a finite number of (possibly overlapping) discs $T_i\subset T$ and disjoint embedded fibered saucers ${}^{T_i}B_i\subset {}^TM$, $i=1,\dots, N$,
 such that  ${}^T\xi_0$ is homotopic rel.\ $(T\times A)\cup \partial T\times M $ to a fibered almost contact structure ${}^T\xi_1$ which is is genuine on ${}^TM\setminus\bigcup B_i$ and whose restriction to each fibered saucer ${}^{T_i}B_i$ is semi-contact and regular.  
 Moreover, we can choose the discs in such a way that any non-empty intersection $T_{i_1}\cap\dots\cap T_{i_k}$, $1\leq i_1<\dots<i_k\leq L$, is again a disc with piecewise smooth boundary.

nodes.name: Lemma 7.2
nodes.statement:
For a closed manifold $\Sigma$, any semi-contact structure  $\xi=\{\zeta_s\}$  on the annulus 
    $C=\Sigma\times[0,1]$ is homotopic relative ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial C$ to an almost contact structure $\widetilde \xi$ which is a genuine contact structure in the complement of   finitely many saucers $B_1,\dots, B_k\subset C$ and such that
    the restriction $\widetilde\xi|_{B_j}$ for $j=1,\dots, k$, 
     is semi-contact and regular.

nodes.name: Theorem 7.1
nodes.statement:
{\rm[M. Gromov, [Gro69, Gr-PDR]]}
 Let $M$ be a $(2n+1)$-manifold,  $A\subset M$ a closed subset, and
  $\xi_0$   a contact structure on  ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A\subset M$. 
  Suppose that  $(M,A)$ is relatively open.
  Then the inclusion $$j:\mathfrak{Cont}(M;A,\xi_0)\to\mathfrak{cont}(M;A,\xi_0)$$ is a homotopy equivalence.
